title: The canonical Weil structure on the constant object is independent of the coefficient stage

source.place: node def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, order 1510 ('equip it with the canonical Weil structure'); the claim was part of the statement of def-weil-constant-weil-structure as written by the worker of def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, and is split off here. Written by an agent

proof.text: Put $g=g_Y$, $F=g^{-1}$, $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$, and $B_m=(A_{L,m})_Y$. The map $g$ is a scheme isomorphism, not assumed to be a $k$-morphism, and $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$ by [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $F$ is an exact equivalence preserving limits; its constant-ring maps $c_A:F(A_Y)\to A_Y$ are ring isomorphisms natural in every ring homomorphism. Write $c_R:FR\to R$ and $c_S:FS\to S$ for their inverse-limit maps as in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. If $\pi^E_m:R\to(A_{E,m})_Y$ and $\pi^L_m:S\to B_m$ are the projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the definitions give $\pi^E_m c_R=c_{A_{E,m}}F\pi^E_m$ and $\pi^L_m c_S=c_{A_{L,m}}F\pi^L_m$.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (proetale-section-morphism); specialization to the geometric-Frobenius isomorphism, with the constant coefficient maps defined in the blueprint coefficient-object paragraph

proof.text:
Let $\iota_m:A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$, $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_m:R\to B_m$, and $j:R\to S$ be the maps of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]; thus $\pi^L_m j=\rho_m$. Naturality of the constant-ring maps from Step 1 gives
$$\rho_m c_R=c_{A_{L,m}}F\rho_m.$$
Indeed, substitute $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_m$ and use naturality for $\iota_m$ and the projection square of Step 1. Composing $c_S F j$ and $j c_R$ with $\pi^L_m$ gives these same maps for every $m$. The coordinate description of the inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] therefore proves
$$c_S F j=j c_R.$$
This checks the coefficient-action square even for ramified extensions: it uses the quotient homomorphisms $\iota_m$, never an identification of the two uniformizers or their powers.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (sites-example-constant-sheaf), functoriality in the constant ring; agent calculation of the completed coefficient square using the displayed projections

proof.text:
Use $R[0]$ as its own K-flat representative: tensoring any acyclic complex with this regular rank-one module gives the same complex, by the tensor definition [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus $R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S=R\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\mu}S$, with $\mu(r\otimes s)=j(r)s$ and inverse $s\mapsto1\otimes s$. The same calculation gives $R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_m=B_m$ with its reduction transitions. By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible], $R,S$ are constructible derived-complete coefficient units. Apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to $K=R$: its natural isomorphism $\chi:R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\to R\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ identifies the strict completed scalar extension with ordinary change of rings. Hence
$$\beta=\mu\chi^{-1}:R\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\xrightarrow{\sim}S.$$
This is the canonical coefficient-unit comparison: at every finite quotient it is $r\otimes b\mapsto\rho_m(r)b$. Its inverse is $\chi\mu^{-1}$: $\mu^{-1}(s)=1\otimes s$, and $\chi$ sends this to the strict-cone point with components $1\otimes\pi^L_m(s)=\pi^L_m(s)$ and zero shifted component. So $\beta$ is the map $\beta_{E,L}$ of the statement, and its image is $\alpha_{E,L}$; since $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ is the limit of a surjective tower, this map is unique with these projections by clause 3 of [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit]. It therefore has exactly the normalization of the scalar-extension isomorphism in clause 3 of the constant-coefficient lemma, rather than an arbitrary unit multiple of that isomorphism.

source.place: Coefficient-object paragraph: scalar extensions of the completed coefficient unit; explicit multiplication on its rank-one models

proof.text: Record the normalization of the derived Weil maps on these unit models. At finite coefficient ring $A$, the pullback of its unit is $F(A_Y)\otimes_{F(A_Y)}A_Y$, with multiplication comparison $x\otimes a\mapsto c_A(x)a$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For $R$, its integral pullback is the strict cone limit of these finite pullbacks [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The augmentations from $FR$ are $F\pi^E_n$, followed by these finite multiplication maps. By Step 1 their composites with the unit identifications are $\pi^E_n c_R$. The tower is therefore the quotient tower of $R$ with this augmentation. Its transitions are epimorphisms: locally a section of a finite constant sheaf is represented by a coefficient, and that coefficient lifts through the surjective ring quotient; these local lifts suffice for epimorphy. The surjective-tower result [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit], clauses 2--3, identifies its cone limit with $R[0]$ and fixes uniquely the map with these projections. Consequently the canonical comparison $\lambda_R:Lg_E^*R\to FR$ of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], followed by $c_R$, is precisely this multiplication-normalized unit map. The same argument applies to $S$ and $L$. These are $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}$ and $\theta_{\mathcal O_L}$ by [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. Thus no choice of an isomorphism between unrelated Roos triangles is being used.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.10, p. 17 (surjective towers); multiplication-normalized constant-unit specialization of the blueprint canonical Weil datum

proof.text:
Compute the scalar comparison before completion. The tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] identifies $F(R\otimes_RS)$ with $FR\otimes_{FR}FS$ and sends $F(r\otimes s)$ to $F(r)\otimes F(s)$. Transporting the coefficients along $c_R,c_S$ is balanced, since Step 2 says $c_S F j=j c_R$. If $\mu_F:FR\otimes_{FR}FS\to FS$ denotes multiplication, the required unit square is
$$c_S\mu_F=\mu(c_R\otimes c_S).$$
On a local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ the left side is $c_S(Fj(x)y)=j(c_R(x))c_S(y)$, which is the right side. Both maps are maps of sheaf tensors: the equality on the sectionwise tensor products descends to their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The identical calculation with $B_m$ and $\rho_m$ gives the square at every finite quotient. The ring reductions commute with each expression because they preserve multiplication and the coefficient homomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EL (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-product-pullback); explicit multiplication calculation of its unit/scalar-extension square

proof.text:
The integral pullback/scalar-extension comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] applies to $f=g$, $K=R$: $g$ is a scheme morphism on schemes where $\ell$ is invertible, and $R$ is in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. It identifies $(Lg_E^*R)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ with $Lg_L^*(R\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)$. On the present unit representatives its tensor comparison is the map of Step 5. To check completion explicitly, use the natural maps $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]: their components are the quotient maps to $B_m$, with zero component in the shifted product of the strict cone. The two routes of Step 5 have equal quotient components for every $m$ and commute with their transitions, so they induce the same map on each product and on both coordinates of its cone. The pullback unit maps are the normalized ones of Step 4, and $\beta$ is the multiplication-normalized map of Step 3. Consequently the integral square is
$$\theta_{\mathcal O_L}\circ Lg_L^*(\beta)=\beta\circ(\theta_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L),$$
with the source identified by that pullback/scalar comparison. This computation only uses rank-one representatives and the stated natural completion maps; it makes no inference from equality of finite reductions of arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Coefficient-object paragraph, canonical Weil structures after coefficient extension; agent calculation on strict quotient/cone models of the two operations

proof.text:
Apply the rationalization functor to the integral square of Step 6. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], its scalar extension is induced on integral representatives by $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$; by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], rational pullback and its comparison are induced from the integral ones. By [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], the images of the integral Weil maps are $\theta_E,\theta_L$. The image of $\beta$ is the canonical $\alpha_{E,L}$ of the statement, so the image square is exactly
$$\theta_L\circ Lg_Y^*(\alpha_{E,L})=\alpha_{E,L}\circ(\theta_E\otimes_EL).$$
This is the morphism condition of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Since $\alpha_{E,L}$ is invertible, its inverse satisfies the reverse condition: multiply this equality by $\alpha_{E,L}^{-1}$ on the left and by $Lg_Y^*(\alpha_{E,L}^{-1})$ on the right. Hence it is an isomorphism of $L$-Weil sheaves. The two underlying objects lie in the constructible heart by [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. This proves clause 1.

source.place: Coefficient-object paragraph, rational coefficient object and its canonical Weil datum; rationalization of the preceding computed square

proof.text: Take the inclusion $\Ql\subset E$ in clause 1. In the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], represent the map from $(\Ql,(\Ql)_Y)$ to $(E,E_Y)$ at the stage $E$ by $\alpha_{\Ql,E}$, inserting the canonical unit identification $E_Y\otimes_EE\cong E_Y$ in the target. Its inverse is represented by $\alpha_{\Ql,E}^{-1}$ with the inverse unit identification. Composing at the same stage gives the two identity classes. The Frobenius-equivariance equation for these representatives is Step 7, since the common-stage pullback acts on representatives with exactly that scalar comparison [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus they are inverse morphisms of $\Qlb$-Weil complexes [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and their underlying objects are precisely the finite-stage representatives specified in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. Inverting this isomorphism gives the direction in clause 2. The forgetful functor sends each representative to its underlying map, so this isomorphism forgets to the canonical coefficient-unit identification. Its normalization is compatible with passing to a larger stage: on the regular module both iterated and direct scalar-unit maps send $(r\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $j(r)st$, and the identity/tower comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] preserve these maps. Therefore it is canonical in the common-stage category. This proves clause 2, without identifying that category of fixed pairs with a derived category of Weil sheaves.
